reading_sub: Fifteen minutes, no dictionary, questions before the text

paras: Rarely is a maritime casualty caused by a single failure, and almost never by a failure of equipment alone. The reports of the last decade point steadily in one direction: what is missing is not the lifeboat but the lifeboat drill, not the certificate but the watchkeeping the certificate is supposed to guarantee.

Under the ISM Code, every company operating a ship must establish procedures for identifying the hazards its own operation creates, and must prepare for the emergencies those hazards make possible. Under STCW, every officer must hold a certificate whose validity depends on periodic revalidation. Neither instrument says anything about a Tuesday afternoon on which the master is ashore, the second officer is on his fourth consecutive watch and the muster station list has not been updated since the last crew change.

Hardly had the industry finished congratulating itself on falling casualty figures when the near-miss data began to tell another story. Near misses are not reported to a flag state and rarely reach an incident report at all, which is precisely why they matter: they are the only record of the accidents that did not happen, and they cluster around exactly the manning arrangements the certificates call adequate.

Not only does under-manning increase fatigue, but it also removes the second person whose whole function is to notice what the first has missed. No amount of documentation replaces that person. Only when the drill is treated as an operation rather than as a record does the paperwork begin to describe the ship.

paras: Artificial intelligence is usually defined as the ability of a digital computer, or of a computer-controlled machine, to perform tasks commonly associated with intelligent beings. The definition is old, and its weakness has always been the word commonly: the tasks we associate with intelligence change as soon as a machine performs one of them.

Not until a program had beaten a reigning world champion at chess did the public accept that a machine could reason at all. Within a decade chess had been reclassified as a problem of search rather than of thought, and the same reclassification has since been applied to translation, to the reading of medical images and to conversation itself.

Research has concentrated on five components: learning, reasoning, problem solving, perception and the use of language. Of these, only learning has produced systems whose behaviour is not entirely specified by the people who built them, and it is for that reason that learning attracts both the investment and the alarm.

Whether such systems can be said to understand anything remains, in the strict sense, undecided. What is no longer in dispute is that they are useful, and that the industries which adopt them soonest tend to be the ones whose work was already written down.

grammar_rows: rarely, seldom, never, little, at no time: the auxiliary jumps in front of the subject
Rarely is a casualty caused by one failure.
one thing had only just happened when the next did
Hardly had they finished when the data changed.
the inversion happens in the FIRST half only; the second half is ordinary
Not only does it increase fatigue, but it also removes...
only when / only after / not until
the inversion lands on the MAIN clause, never inside the only-clause
Only when the drill is real does the paperwork describe the ship.

inversion is EMPHASIS, not negation. Rarely is a casualty caused by a single failure does not mean never. Turning rarely into never, or hardly into not at all, is the standard wrong option -- and it is wrong by degree, not by topic.
grammar_insight: Inversion tells you the writer is leaning on something. It never tells you the thing is absolute. Every question built on an inverted sentence tests whether you read the degree or only the direction.

quickfire.situation: Rarely is a casualty caused by a single failure. Does the writer say it never is?
tips: No. Rarely is emphasis, not negation.
An option that says never is wrong by degree, not by topic.

quickfire.situation: The AI text says chess was reclassified. From what to what, and why does it matter to the writer?

quickfire.situation: An option says: the text states that these systems understand what they read. Is that supported?

listenings.sub: An examiner explains where the marks are actually lost. Sound first -- no text.
listenings.text: Candidates lose marks in three places, and only one of them is vocabulary. The first is degree. The text says rarely and the option says never, and because the topic is identical the eye accepts it. The second is agency. The text says the figures must have been produced from another plan, and the option says the operator produced them from another plan, and the difference is the whole sentence. The third is register. The text says the vessel ran aground and the option says the vessel became hard-fast, and the candidate rejects the right answer precisely because it does not look like the text. If you fix those three, you do not need to read faster. You already read well enough.
questions: What are the three places candidates lose marks?
Degree, agency and register. Only one of the three is really about vocabulary.
What example does she give for degree?
The text says rarely and the option says never. Because the topic is identical, the eye accepts it.
Why does she say a candidate rejects the right answer on register?
Because the correct option is written in different words from the text, so it does not look like the text.

listenings.sub: A safety officer on the difference between a record and an operation. Sound first -- no text.
listenings.text: I have signed hundreds of drill records and I have watched perhaps a third of the drills they describe. That is the whole problem in one sentence. On paper we hold a lifeboat drill every month and every person on board has a muster station. In practice, a drill that takes eleven minutes and ends with everyone back at work has taught nobody anything. What I look for now is different. I want to see somebody sent to the wrong station on purpose. I want the list to be wrong and somebody to notice. And I want the near miss written down even when nothing happened, because the near miss is the only honest record we keep. Nobody is ever punished for an accident that did not occur, which is exactly why people will tell you about it.
questions: What does he say about the drill records he has signed?
He has signed hundreds of them and watched perhaps a third of the drills they describe.
What is wrong with a drill that takes eleven minutes?
It ends with everyone back at work and it has taught nobody anything. It is a record rather than an operation.
Why does he say near misses are the only honest record?
Because nobody is ever punished for an accident that did not occur, which is exactly why people will tell you about it.

quiz.q: Rarely is a maritime casualty caused by a single failure. What does the sentence claim?

quiz.q: Why is it Not only does under-manning increase fatigue and not Not only under-manning increases fatigue?
opts: Because the negative phrase at the front pulls the auxiliary in front of the subject.
Because under-manning is plural.
Because not only can never be followed by a noun.

quiz.q: In Only when the drill is treated as an operation does the paperwork begin..., where does the inversion happen?
opts: Inside the only when clause.
In the main clause, after the only when clause has finished.
In both halves of the sentence.

grammar_tip_title: Inversion After Negative and Limiting Adverbials
grammar_tip_lead: Formal prose puts the emphatic word first and pays for it by moving the auxiliary in front of the subject. Nothing about the facts changes -- but the degree does, and the degree is what the wrong option attacks.

teacher.s1: Abertura (1 min): Esta e a aula de SIMULADO que fecha o bloco 1. DECISAO DE DESENHO do programa: toda aula e reading-driven (a REGRA 29.2 nao se aplica aqui), porque a prova e 100% leitura. Hoje o formato e o da prova de verdade: DOIS textos, um deles sem nenhum navio. Entre direto, sem cumprimento scriptado (REGRA 27A).
teacher.s2: Warm-up (3 min): Antes do relogio: qual das quatro mecanicas do bloco 1 ainda custa mais tempo a ela. Anote a resposta e compare no debrief -- e provavel que nao seja a mesma que os erros vao mostrar.
teacher.s3: Provocacao (4 min): A frase e a primeira linha do texto 1 e ja e o assunto do capitulo 4. Peca o que a frase diz E o que ela NAO diz. Se ela responder 'never', voce acabou de encontrar o erro mais caro da prova.
teacher.s4: Objetivo (1 min): Diga: two texts, ten questions, and a debrief that is about reasons, not about the score.
teacher.s5: Transicao vocab (1 min): Diga: Ten words that place a text inside the regulatory system. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s6: Vocab reveal 1-4 (5 min): incident report, near miss, master, flag state. NAO traduza (REGRA 13). CCQ para near miss: If nothing happened, why write it down? (Porque e o unico registro dos acidentes que NAO aconteceram -- e o argumento do texto.) CCQ para master: Is the master the owner? (Nao -- e quem comanda.)
teacher.s7: Vocab reveal 5-7 (5 min): manning, watchkeeping, STCW. CCQ para manning: Is manning about how many, or about who? (Os dois: numero E qualificacao.) Diga o que a sigla STCW significa uma vez, devagar, e nao volte a ela: o que importa e reconhecer, nao decorar.
teacher.s8: Vocab reveal 8-10 (5 min): ISM Code, muster station, lifeboat drill. CCQ para ISM Code: Is the ISM Code about equipment? (Nao -- sobre PROCEDIMENTO. E a diferenca que o texto explora.) Peca que ela diga a diferenca entre ISM e STCW em uma frase.
teacher.s9: Consolidate (4 min): Ela toca a palavra e le a definicao em voz alta antes de fechar o par.
teacher.s10: Transicao (1 min): Diga: The clock starts now. Fifteen minutes for this text and its questions. O proximo slide e o de TAREFA: as perguntas ANTES do texto.
teacher.s11: Texto 1 -- SOB RELOGIO (8 min): Cronometre de verdade e diga o tempo em voz alta a cada 5 minutos. NAO ajude, NAO traduza, NAO responda pergunta durante. Anote onde ela para. E o unico momento do programa em que voce fica calado.
teacher.s12: Gist (2 min): Ela escolhe e justifica. A opcao (c) e a inversao do que o texto diz e existe para punir leitura rapida.
teacher.s13: True or False (5 min): Ainda sob relogio. Ela responde as cinco e SO DEPOIS voces conferem. A afirmacao 1 e a de GRAU (seldom x never) e a 2 e a de ESCOPO (limitada a registros).
teacher.s14: Transicao gramatica (1 min): Diga: The first line of that text is a structure, and it is the one that costs marks. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s15: Grammar discovery (6 min): Nao de a regra. Peca que ela reescreva o exemplo 1 em ordem normal, em voz alta, e diga o que mudou. So entao clique Reveal the Rule. CCQ decisivo: Rarely is a casualty caused by one failure -- does the writer say never? (Nao.) Ela estuda gramatica sozinha: aqui e ferramenta de leitura, nao producao.
teacher.s16: Practice (3 min): Ela diz a forma ORALMENTE antes de clicar.
teacher.s17: Spot the error (3 min): Os quatro sao falta de inversao -- o erro que um falante de portugues comete porque em portugues a ordem nao muda.
teacher.s18: Transicao equivalencia (1 min): Diga: Same two texts, other words. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s19: Como a prova esconde (3 min): Os quatro pares saiam dos DOIS textos. O quarto par (remains undecided -> the question is still open) e o que mais cai.
teacher.s20: Equivalencia (4 min): Depois de fechar os pares, cubra a direita e faca a direcao dificil.
teacher.s21: Complete (4 min): Teacher-led, uma lacuna por vez. As oito respostas sao oito das dez palavras da aula.
teacher.s22: Quick fire (5 min): Uma por vez, em voz alta, antes das dicas. A primeira e a quinta sao as duas que valem ponto na prova.
teacher.s22a: Texto 2 -- SOB RELOGIO (7 min): Este texto NAO tem navio nenhum, e isso e deliberado: a prova de 2025 abriu com um texto de Inteligencia Artificial da Britannica. Cronometre. NAO ajude. Se ela reclamar que 'nao e do assunto', essa e exatamente a reclamacao que a prova produz -- anote e use no debrief.
teacher.s22b: True or False do texto 2 (5 min): Mesma regra da casa: TRUE ou FALSE e DEPOIS a linha que prova, em voz alta. A afirmacao 4 (understand) e a de GRAU: undecided nao e sim e nao e nao.
teacher.s23: Transicao debrief (1 min): Diga: Now the part that is worth more than the score. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s24: Listening 1 (5 min): LEIA AS 3 PERGUNTAS EM VOZ ALTA COM ELA ANTES de tocar (REGRA 2.1). Escuta medida em 0%: 0.75x na primeira vez. Este audio nomeia as tres perdas (degree, agency, register) -- peca que ela repita as tres sem olhar e diga em qual das tres ela caiu hoje.
teacher.s25: Listening 2 (5 min): LEIA AS 3 PERGUNTAS EM VOZ ALTA COM ELA ANTES de tocar (REGRA 2.1). Este e o lado humano do texto 1. No fim pergunte: he says the near miss is the only honest record. Does the written text say the same thing? (Diz -- com outras palavras, e essa e a aula toda.)
teacher.s26: Debrief guiado (5 min): Tres questoes, com a linha de evidencia e o defeito de cada distrator. NAO deixe passar 'achei que era essa' -- exija a linha.
teacher.s27: Debrief semi-livre (5 min): Ela DEFENDE a opcao errada. E o exercicio mais valioso do bloco: quem sabe montar o distrator para de cair nele.
teacher.s28: Producao livre (5 min): Nao interrompa. Mede-se: ela nomeia tres passos do proprio metodo, em ordem. Se ela nao tiver metodo nomeavel, ESSE e o achado da aula e vira o foco do bloco 2.
teacher.s29: Transicao wrap-up (1 min): Diga: Block one, closed.
teacher.s30: Survival card (3 min): As cinco frases sao as cinco inversoes dos dois textos. Toque e peca repeticao -- dizer em voz alta e o que fixa a ORDEM invertida.
